candidates.title: Masked L1 training loss to match the absolute-error metric
candidates.rationale: The fixed independent scorer is disk-masked absolute error, but training_loss minimizes squared error. Squared-error regression estimates the conditional mean, while the predictor that minimizes expected absolute error is the conditional median; when forecast residuals are skewed or heavy-tailed, the mean-optimal predictor carries avoidable MAE. The evidence is consistent with this objective/metric mismatch: masked MSE flattens near 0.033-0.036 after ~step 20, yet validation MAE is 0.1221 versus persistence 0.1265 (skill 0.034), i.e. the converged L2 solution barely improves the MAE metric. Also, L2 gradients shrink proportionally to error magnitude and go quiet late in training, wasting part of the fixed 40-step budget, whereas L1 keeps constant-magnitude gradients throughout. The edit is one line in training_loss; build_model, fit, and config steps/batch_size/seed are untouched, and CPU cost is identical. This is a hypothesis to be confirmed on the held-out split, not a claimed measured gain.
candidates.diff:
--- previous/candidate.py
+++ proposed/candidate.py
@@ -25,7 +25,7 @@
 
 
 def training_loss(prediction,target,mask):
-    return ((prediction-target).square()*mask).sum()/mask.sum()
+    return ((prediction-target).abs()*mask).sum()/mask.sum()
 
 
 def fit(model,x,y,mask,config):

candidates.title: Zero-init the residual head so training starts at persistence
candidates.rationale: The residual head returns net(x)+x[:,1:2], so the conv stack only has to learn the correction to the persistence channel. With default random init, the final 3x3 conv emits a random field of nonzero magnitude at step 0, so training starts worse than persistence and the earliest of the 40 config-fixed steps (batch 8) are spent canceling initialization noise instead of fitting the correction - consistent with the slim 0.034 skill over persistence after training. Zero-initializing the final conv's weight and bias makes the step-0 prediction exactly persistence (the 0.1265-error baseline by construction) while gradients through that conv remain nonzero, so every step optimizes the correction from a clean starting point; this is the standard zero-init trick for residual image-to-image heads. The edit is two init lines gated on architecture=='residual'; loss, interfaces, and config steps/batch_size/seed are untouched. Hypothesis to be verified on held-out data, not a claimed measured gain.
candidates.diff:
--- previous/candidate.py
+++ proposed/candidate.py
@@ -18,6 +18,9 @@
             self.net=nn.Sequential(nn.Conv2d(2,width,3,padding=1),nn.ReLU(),
                                    nn.Conv2d(width,width,3,padding=1),nn.ReLU(),
                                    nn.Conv2d(width,1,3,padding=1))
+            if architecture=='residual':
+                nn.init.zeros_(self.net[4].weight)
+                nn.init.zeros_(self.net[4].bias)
         def forward(self,x):
             prediction=self.net(x)
             return prediction+x[:,1:2] if architecture=='residual' else prediction

decision.title: Select the tested zero-init residual head (validation error 0.1221→0.1114); defer L1 composition as untested
decision.rationale: Both candidates were run against the same baseline (validation error 0.12212, persistence 0.12645) with identical config (steps 40, batch_size 8, seed 17) and an identical fit loop, so the seeded generator draws the same batch-index sequence in every run and each comparison is paired. Masked-L1 loss reached 0.12055 (skill 0.034→0.047), a small measured gain. Zero-initializing the residual head's final conv reached 0.11143 (skill 0.034→0.119), an ~8.8% error reduction and the largest measured change. Mechanistically, the zero-init edit makes the step-0 prediction exactly the persistence channel x[:,1:2], so none of the 40 fixed steps is spent canceling random-init noise and every step fits the correction; since nn.init.zeros_ consumes no RNG, all other layers keep their baseline initialization, isolating the cause of the gain. I therefore select the zero-init candidate as the new source. I deliberately do not also adopt the L1 loss: the L1 reading was taken without zero-init, so that composition is untested and cannot be described as an improvement; L1-on-top-of-zero-init remains the natural next single-change experiment. KEEP is rejected because it would discard a measured, mechanism-level gain from a two-line change.
decision.lesson: Start a residual predictor at its known baseline: zero-initializing the head so the model begins at persistence converted early optimizer steps from noise-cancelation into learning and produced the largest measured validation gain; testing one change per run with matched seed and batch sampling makes credit assignment unambiguous.
decision.limits: Evidence is validation-only (142 examples, one seed, 40 steps); final test data and scores are unavailable, so the 0.11143 reading may not transfer. The L1+zero-init composition is untested and could interact (L1's constant-magnitude sign gradients behave differently from MSE's error-scaled gradients on a zero-init head). Zero-init is gated to architecture='residual'; the mlp/conv1d paths and the non-residual image path keep random init and were not re-evaluated.

candidates.title: Masked-L1 training loss aligned with the scored metric
candidates.rationale: The fixed independent metric is disk-masked absolute error, but training minimizes masked squared error: MSE concentrates gradient on large-error pixels and targets the conditional mean, while the metric weights every masked pixel equally and is minimized by the conditional median. This one-line swap (.square() to .abs()) makes the descent objective match the scored quantity, the most direct available lever on learner_metric. The recorded lesson flags the L1 x zero-init composition as untested: on the zero-initialized residual head, L1 yields sign(residual) gradients of constant magnitude even where residuals are already small, unlike MSE error-scaled gradients. Under Adam that magnitude difference is largely normalized away (per-parameter steps are about lr either way), so the start-at-persistence behavior should be preserved; the open question is whether uniform per-pixel pressure beats error-weighted pressure on this metric. Model, fit loop, seed 17 and batch sampling are untouched, so any validation movement against the recorded 0.11143 is attributable to the loss alone. No improvement is claimed; note the returned loss curve changes scale (roughly 0.1-range values) and is not comparable to the old MSE curve.

-    return ((prediction-target).square()*mask).sum()/mask.sum()
+    # masked mean absolute error, matching the fixed disk-masked absolute error metric
+    return ((prediction-target).abs()*mask).sum()/mask.sum()
 
 
 def fit(model,x,y,mask,config):

candidates.title: Keep zero-init residual head with masked MSE
candidates.rationale: Keep the only configuration with a measured gain: validation error 0.11143 versus persistence 0.12645 (skill 0.119), produced by the zero-init residual head under masked MSE at seed 17 over 40 steps on 142 validation examples. The lesson explicitly marks the L1 x zero-init combination as untested with a plausible adverse interaction: constant-magnitude sign gradients keep pushing head outputs that are already nearly correct, which can add churn late in a short 40-step budget, whereas the zero-init benefit was established under error-scaled MSE gradients. Changing the loss alters the gradient field that measured gain depended on, and with a single seed and a small validation set the noise floor is unknown; no evidence yet shows the MSE/MAE mismatch costs anything measurable. KEEP changes nothing and claims no improvement; it preserves the validated setup and leaves the metric-alignment experiment to run later as its own clean, seed-matched comparison against the recorded 0.11143.

decision.title: Adopt the tested metric-aligned masked-L1 loss on the zero-init head (validation 0.1114→0.1109)
decision.rationale: The composition flagged last round as untested (masked-L1 on top of the zero-init residual head) has now been run as its own single-change experiment: candidate accb1bc5 differs from the current source only in training_loss (.square() to .abs()); the model, zero-init head, fit loop, seed 17 and batch sampling are identical, so the seeded generator draws the same batch-index sequence and the comparison is paired. The KEEP re-run (ac31adea) reproduced the incumbent validation error exactly (0.11143358542213977), confirming the pipeline is deterministic under the fixed config, so the delta between the two candidates is attributable to the loss change rather than harness jitter. Measured result: masked-L1 reached 0.11092 versus 0.11143 for masked-MSE, a reduction of about 0.0005 absolute error (roughly 0.5 percent relative; skill vs persistence 0.1188 to 0.1229). The mechanism predicts this direction: the fixed independent metric is disk-masked absolute error, and training now descends exactly that quantity instead of a squared-error surrogate that concentrates gradient on large-error pixels and targets the conditional mean. The adverse interaction flagged last round did not materialize: the L1 curve declines smoothly from 0.125 to about 0.11 with no late churn, and under Adam per-parameter step sizes are largely lr-normalized, so constant-magnitude sign gradients preserve the zero-init start-at-persistence behavior. I therefore select the L1-plus-zero-init source as the new baseline. I claim no more than the evidence shows: the margin is small and single-seed, the two loss curves live on different scales (L1 around 0.11, MSE around 0.03) and are not comparable to each other, and only the validation metric was compared. KEEP is rejected because it would discard the only measured improvement available, from a one-line, zero-cost change that preserves all interfaces. Any further composition (loss reweighting, Huber, capacity, longer schedules) remains untested and must be run alone against the newly recorded 0.11092.

lessons.lesson: Align the training objective with the scored metric: swapping masked-MSE for masked-L1 — the same absolute error the fixed metric computes — converted the previously untested L1×zero-init composition into a measured paired gain (0.11143 → 0.11092, skill 0.1188 → 0.1229) with no added cost or interface change; a deterministic re-run of the incumbent (identical 0.11143) is what makes the single-change attribution clean, and the feared constant-magnitude sign-gradient churn on the zero-init head did not appear under Adam.
lessons.limits: Evidence is validation-only (142 examples, one seed, 40 steps); the ~0.0005 margin is small enough that it may not replicate under other seeds, and final test data and scores are unavailable. decision.lesson: Align the training objective with the scored metric: swapping masked-MSE for masked-L1 — the same absolute error the fixed metric computes — converted the previously untested L1×zero-init composition into a measured paired gain (0.11143 → 0.11092, skill 0.1188 → 0.1229) with no added cost or interface change; a deterministic re-run of the incumbent (identical 0.11143) is what makes the single-change attribution clean, and the feared constant-magnitude sign-gradient churn on the zero-init head did not appear under Adam.

adopted.title: Adopt the tested metric-aligned masked-L1 loss on the zero-init head (validation 0.1114→0.1109)
adopted.rationale: The composition flagged last round as untested (masked-L1 on top of the zero-init residual head) has now been run as its own single-change experiment: candidate accb1bc5 differs from the current source only in training_loss (.square() to .abs()); the model, zero-init head, fit loop, seed 17 and batch sampling are identical, so the seeded generator draws the same batch-index sequence and the comparison is paired. The KEEP re-run (ac31adea) reproduced the incumbent validation error exactly (0.11143358542213977), confirming the pipeline is deterministic under the fixed config, so the delta between the two candidates is attributable to the loss change rather than harness jitter. Measured result: masked-L1 reached 0.11092 versus 0.11143 for masked-MSE, a reduction of about 0.0005 absolute error (roughly 0.5 percent relative; skill vs persistence 0.1188 to 0.1229). The mechanism predicts this direction: the fixed independent metric is disk-masked absolute error, and training now descends exactly that quantity instead of a squared-error surrogate that concentrates gradient on large-error pixels and targets the conditional mean. The adverse interaction flagged last round did not materialize: the L1 curve declines smoothly from 0.125 to about 0.11 with no late churn, and under Adam per-parameter step sizes are largely lr-normalized, so constant-magnitude sign gradients preserve the zero-init start-at-persistence behavior. I therefore select the L1-plus-zero-init source as the new baseline. I claim no more than the evidence shows: the margin is small and single-seed, the two loss curves live on different scales (L1 around 0.11, MSE around 0.03) and are not comparable to each other, and only the validation metric was compared. KEEP is rejected because it would discard the only measured improvement available, from a one-line, zero-cost change that preserves all interfaces. Any further composition (loss reweighting, Huber, capacity, longer schedules) remains untested and must be run alone against the newly recorded 0.11092.
